assessment: Out-of-order completions and unexpected source versions support testing a joint identity-and-scheduling change. They do not establish whether queueing or editor selection accounts for the ten slower sessions. One opening is warranted; meeting the time target remains unproven.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: cross immutable video-caption manifests with generation-aware pending-render coalescing at the save-to-render-queue interface. Each save records both source hashes and a request generation; only the newest pending generation is dispatched. Completion publishes against its captured manifest, while a current-preview pointer advances only to the still-intended generation. Preserve the delivered version and original captions through a separate retained pointer.
openings.delta: Manifest binding alone leaves redundant render demand; coalescing alone cannot establish which video-caption pair a completion contains. Together, the same identity determines both work eligibility and preview eligibility, potentially reducing wasted work without making arrival order stand for editorial intent.
openings.prediction: In multi-save sessions with overlapping jobs, the combination should reduce obsolete renders relative to manifest binding alone and reduce incorrectly identified previews relative to coalescing alone. Jointly correct-and-timely previews should improve most where both overlap and identity confusion occur; little benefit is expected in single-correction sessions. If selection or watching dominates, the time target may remain unmet.
openings.probe: Use fabricated footage and timestamped events in private staging to compare baseline, manifest-only, coalescing-only, and combined behavior under identical rapid-save, reversed-completion, and changed-cut sequences. Measure obsolete dispatches, actual output source hashes, editor identification errors, and waiting versus selection time. Verify retained delivered wording and playable embedded-caption output. Bound implementation to four engineer-days and editor comparison to one editor-day; record processing use. Subsequently evaluate the stated 30-session target: at least 27 correctly identified within 15 minutes and zero unintended combinations.
assumptions: Workers can capture and verify immutable input pairs with a small queue/publication change.
Enough redundant requests remain pending for coalescing to save processing.
Retained manifests and source captions fit existing private storage; staging plus normal work remains within 80 processing hours per week.
